rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Cabo Rojo County in Puerto Rico...
Hormigueros County in Puerto Rico...
Western Maricao County in Puerto Rico...
Eastern Mayaguez County in Puerto Rico...
Sabana Grande County in Puerto Rico...
San German County in Puerto Rico...

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Hardin,
Jasper, Jefferson and Orange Counties.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Village Creek Near Kountze affecting Hardin County.

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

For the Neches River...including Town Bluff, Evadale, Neches River
Saltwater Barrier...Moderate flooding is forecast.
For the Village Creek...including Kountze...Major flooding is
forecast.
For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight CDT.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Village Creek near Kountze.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Major lowland flooding will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 11.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 23.3 feet just after midnight
tonight. It will then fall below flood stage early tomorrow
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 23.9
feet on 05/09/1969.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
At 1222 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near Fountainhead-Orchard Hills to near Carroll Valley
to 6 miles northeast of Hampstead to near Brogue, moving southeast at
40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Damaging winds will cause some trees and large branches to
fall. This could injure those outdoors, as well as damage
homes and vehicles. Roadways may become blocked by downed
trees. Localized power outages are possible. Unsecured
light objects may become projectiles.

Locations impacted include...
Frederick, Hagerstown, Cockeysville, Westminster, Thurmont,
Emmitsburg, Municipal Stadium, Eldersburg, Reisterstown, Robinwood,
Taneytown, Hampstead, Walkersville, Fountainhead-Orchard Hills,
Manchester, Boonsboro, Smithsburg, Jarrettsville, Paramount-Long
Meadow, and Wilson-Conococheague.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Hardin, TX; Jasper, TX; Tyler, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1121 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain in Reports of flood have been
received from Tyler and Hardin Counties. Between 5 and 20 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.25 to 0.5 inches in
1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lumberton, Silsbee, Woodville, Kountze, Sour Lake, Colmesneil,
Chester, Wildwood, Warren, Fred, Thicket, Saratoga, Town Bluff,
Village Mills, Honey Island, Caney Head, Spurger, Votaw and Batson.

Rainfall has generally tapered off to a much lighter rainfall than
earlier this morning. However numerous roads remain flooded and
closed across the warned area as water continues to drain.

possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east-central Texas, including the following
counties, Henderson, Anderson, Freestone and Leon.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
